knocker.yt_title: Before Alarm Clocks, She Shot Peas at You #shorts
knocker.yt_desc:
Before cheap alarm clocks, factory workers in Britain paid a 'knocker-up' to wake them. In London's East End, Mary Smith did it with a pea shooter, for sixpence a week.

Would you pay sixpence for a pea at your window? A or B 👇

Sources:
• Wikipedia, Knocker-up (tools, pea shooter photo of Mary Smith, decline): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knocker-up
• Atlas Obscura, Remembering the 'Knocker-Ups' (sixpence a week, 3 AM rounds, rival with a fishing rod, grumpy vs musical reply taps): https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/what-did-people-use-before-alarm-clocks
• Mental Floss, the job of waking people before alarm clocks (daughter kept working through air raids; a knocker-up who saved a family from a burning house): https://www.mentalfloss.com/history/surprising-job-waking-people-up-before-alarm-clocks

bats.yt_title: How Bats Burned Down Their Own Base #shorts
bats.yt_desc:
A dentist pitched a plan to fight a war with bats carrying tiny fire bombs, and it was approved. Then, at a desert air base, armed bats escaped.

If you were the general: A, keep the bats, or B, buy a new car? 👇

Sources:
• Wikipedia, Bat bomb (Lytle S. Adams, Mexican free-tailed bats, 'This man is not a nut', ice cube trays, 1,040 bats per carrier, Carlsbad accident, about $2 million, cancelled as too slow): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat_bomb
• Air & Space Forces Magazine, The Bat Bombers (escaped bats set fire to a hangar and a general's car; bombs clipped to the bats): https://www.airandspaceforces.com/article/1090bats/

The skeptic officer's lines are a dramatized retelling; the facts are from the sources above.
